title: GTA 6 Was Never Going to Hit 60 Frames per Second on Consoles
description: IGN reports that GTA 6 targets 30 fps on all consoles, including the PS5 Pro. Gameplay footage and official confirmation show it was never meant to run at 60 fps.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Was Never Going to Hit 60 Frames per Second on Consoles

As anticipation for Rockstar Games' upcoming masterpiece continues to reach fever pitch, technical discussions surrounding performance targets have been a constant talking point. According to a recent report by IGN, the question of whether the game would run at 60 frames per second on consoles has finally been put to rest, with clear indications that it was never in the cards.

### Reading Between the Lines of Gameplay Footage

Back when Rockstar first showcased a significant amount of GTA 6 gameplay via Netflix, a crucial detail stood out to eagle-eyed fans and technical analysts alike: the game was clearly operating at around 30 fps. 

Now, with Rockstar officially confirming that it is targeting a 30 fps performance standard across every single console—including the high-end PS5 Pro—it has become blatantly obvious that the ambitious open-world title likely never would have been able to maintain a solid 60 fps on console hardware.

### Pushing Open-World Boundaries

As one of the most technically demanding projects in video game history, GTA 6 aims to deliver an unprecedented level of fidelity, from intricate physics and dense crowd behaviors to breathtaking lighting models and massive map scale. These elements place an immense load on console hardware architecture.

While mid-generation hardware refreshes like the PS5 Pro offer substantial GPU boosts, developers must constantly balance resolution, graphical fidelity, and performance targets. Rockstar’s choice to target 30 fps highlights their dedication to maximizing visual splendor and world density over high frame rates, prioritizing an immersive cinematic experience.

### Editor's Take

While high-framerate purists might initially balk at the 30 fps lock, Rockstar's history proves that stable frame pacing and rich, uncompromised world simulation matter far more for their style of games. If the 30 fps target delivers a rock-solid, visually stunning experience, it remains a worthwhile trade-off for gaming's biggest release.
